subject: how two shared-control Toffoli gates are decomposed, reordered via commutation rules, and parallelized into Fanout gates

groups.why_chosen: Two Toffoli gates sharing one control qubit would normally run sequentially; decomposing each into T-gates and then using commutation rules to push matching-control CNOTs together turns them into parallel Fanout gates, cutting circuit depth without changing the T-depth.
groups.what_to_learn: consistent two-colour shading tracking which of two originally-sequential operations a gate belongs to, carried across multiple panels of a derivation; a small 'rule' panel of equivalent circuit fragments used to justify a reordering applied in a following panel; a numbered step axis over a quantum circuit to make parallel execution explicit
